text: a rain gauge works by funneling precipitation into a small measuring tube. its top opening is made wider than the tube on purpose. if the mouth has say ten times the area of the inner tube, a single inch of rain fills the tube to ten inches. its an amplifier, lets you read a hundredth of an inch really precisely. not always accurate though. evaporation is a big one, the water can dry out of the tube before you measure it, in warm or windy conditions. wind causes issues too with turbulence up above the mouth, where it knocks rain off to one side. that can cause a huge error on an actual gauge.
